newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia plans to make vans in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Kia plans to make vans in Indonesia.

text.p: South Korea's Kia Motors Corp said on Tuesday it planned to manufacture 50,000 utility vans a year from 1998 with Indonesia's PT Timor Putra Nasional, in Indonesia.

"After discussions with our joint venture partner PT Timor Putra Nasional and the Indonsian government, we have agreed on a plan to include production of utility vans to Indonesia's national car project," Kia's executive vice president Kim Seung-ahn said.
PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by President Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, and Kia have officially launched Indonesia's national passenger car "Timor" on October 1.
Timor, a four-door 1,600cc sedan, is currently made in South Korea and imported, but will eventually be manufactured in Indonesia.

"The production capacity of the national car plant, which is scheduled to have an annual capacity of 70,000 vehicles, could rise to 120,000 if we go ahead with the plan to make vans," said Kim. "The plant is scheduled for completion by early 1998."
The construction of the plant will start this month.
Kim said the utility vans are also expected to enjoy tax and tariff breaks like the Timor.
